text:
erin: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — recurring p95 spike on model-serving during small-batch backfills. Need to lock remediation owners, timeline, and SLO changes. Can folks ack and propose owners by EOD?

sam: TL;DR: spikes happen during cache warmups / small-batch fanout around 03:15 UTC. p95 jumps from ~90ms -> ~450ms, p99 worse. Error budget burn ~0.6%/day on affected route. Traces show KV cache pressure and batching interaction.

jules: Saw the same traces. Dashboard slice here: https://redwood/dashboards/model-serving/latency (will add pinned tiles). Current alerts are pretty broad.

mike: I can own the batching/routing remediation (config + prototype). ETA 2 weeks for prototype + perf numbers.

erin: Thanks Mike. Jules, can you own dashboard + alert tuning (make the batch slice explicit and add burn-rate alert)? Sam, can you own RCA document + timeline? I'll own the postmortem update + product notification.

oncall-bot: Postmortem created: https://redwood/postmortems/2026-03-model-serving-p95-spike — assigned to @erin.

sam: Proposal for SLO adjustments: either a) increase p95 SLO from 100ms -> 200ms for the general route, OR b) introduce tiered SLOs and routing so interactive traffic keeps p95 <= 120ms while batch gets p95 <= 400ms. Prefer (b).

jules: I prefer tiered SLOs too. Suggest explicit policy:
```
interactive: p95 <= 120ms
batch-job-api: p95 <= 400ms
error-budget-alert: burn-rate > 0.4%/day
```

erin: We can't relax interactive SLO. If routing to separate pool is feasible, keep interactive at current SLO and move batch to separate pool/SLO. Mike — can you estimate infra delta?

mike: Rough estimate: separate batch pool (low-priority GPUs + different autoscale) ~ +12% infra cost, should cut interactive p95 spikes by ~60% in simulations. I'll put numbers in the prototype doc.

sam: Action items (recap):
- mike: prototype routing + cost estimate (deliverable: PR + perf runbook) — due 2026-04-08
- jules: dashboard slices, new alerts, runbook snippet for batch incidents — due 2026-03-31
- erin: update postmortem with SLO decision + notify Product & CS — due 2026-03-29
- sam: full RCA write-up + trace links + incident timeline — due 2026-03-30

erin: Weekly stabilization check-in Wednesdays 10:00 PT until we hit 14 days without recurrence. I'll add to calendar and invite owners.

jules: Adding alerts: p95 > 250ms over 5m for the route and error-budget burn > 0.4%/day. Will add dashboard link and a short playbook entry.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled for routing prototype on 2026-04-01 03:00 UTC. Watch logs: /canaries/model-routing/proto-1

sam: Noting this is recurring — similar bursts on 2025-12-07 and 2026-01-22. I'll include timeline table in the RCA so we can spot pattern triggers.

erin: Also pinging Security for KMS permission check for metrics export to our on-prem analytics (DMing).

mike: If prototype validates, we can automate routing: when batch-queue-depth > X and burn-rate > Y, route new batch requests to batch-pool. Ops implications: throttling + extra capacity.

jules: Question — do we add an automatic throttle action in SLO policy (QAction) to pause noncritical experiments when burn > threshold? That would be a quick safety valve.

erin: Possibly. Need Product sign-off on automatic throttle for user-facing impact. I'll loop in @product-ops once we have the cost/impact numbers.

sam: I'll draft the SLO change proposal (with alternatives and rollback plan) and ping infra leadership by EOD.

jules: Linking current dashboard for reference: https://redwood/dashboards/model-serving/p95-trends

erin: Great. Thanks everyone — adding owners to the postmortem doc and calendar invite now. Please update your deliverable when you have PRs or docs so I can mark progress.

mike: Ack. Starting prototyping tomorrow.

jules: ack :thumbsup:

erin: Closing loop: can we reconvene in this thread with links only (PRs/docs) to keep noise down? I'll call out any blockers.

sam: will do — I'll post RCA + timeline table here when ready.

oncall-bot: Reminder: weekly SLO check-in scheduled 2026-03-25 17:00 UTC (recurring).
